data.title: Results: Bilibili Inc. Exceeded Expectations And The Consensus Has Updated Its Estimates
data.description:
Investors in Bilibili Inc. (NASDAQ:BILI) had a good week, as its shares rose 7.8% to close at US$11.43 following the release of its third-quarter results. Bilibili reported CN¥8.3b in revenue, roughly in line with analyst forecasts, although statutory earnings per share (EPS) of CN¥1.14 beat expectations, being 7.6% higher than what the analysts expected. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We thought readers would find it interesting to see the analysts latest (statutory) post-earnings forecasts for next year.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

After the latest results, the 32 analysts covering Bilibili are now predicting revenues of CN¥35.6b in 2027. If met, this would reflect a solid 11% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to shoot up 36% to CN¥5.23. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of CN¥36.1b and earnings per share (EPS) of CN¥5.50 in 2027. The analysts seem to have become a little more negative on the business after the latest results, given the small dip in their earnings per share numbers for next year.

See our latest analysis for Bilibili

The average price target fell 18% to US$20.30, with reduced earnings forecasts clearly tied to a lower valuation estimate. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. The most optimistic Bilibili analyst has a price target of US$35.97 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at US$11.40. Even so, with a relatively close grouping of estimates, it looks like the analysts are quite confident in their valuations, suggesting Bilibili is an easy business to forecast or the the analysts are all using similar assumptions.

One way to get more context on these forecasts is to look at how they compare to both past performance, and how other companies in the same industry are performing. It's pretty clear that there is an expectation that Bilibili's revenue growth will slow down substantially, with revenues to the end of 2027 expected to display 8.8% growth on an annualised basis. This is compared to a historical growth rate of 11% over the past five years. By way of comparison, the other companies in this industry with analyst coverage are forecast to grow their revenue at 18% per year. So it's pretty clear that, while revenue growth is expected to slow down, the wider industry is also expected to grow faster than Bilibili.

The Bottom Line

The biggest concern is that the analysts reduced their earnings per share estimates, suggesting business headwinds could lay ahead for Bilibili. On the plus side, there were no major changes to revenue estimates; although forecasts imply they will perform worse than the wider industry. The consensus price target fell measurably, with the analysts seemingly not reassured by the latest results, leading to a lower estimate of Bilibili's future valuation.

With that said, the long-term trajectory of the company's earnings is a lot more important than next year. At Simply Wall St, we have a full range of analyst estimates for Bilibili going out to 2028, and you can see them free on our platform here..

KROP leans heavily toward Agricultural and Farm Machinery at 39.7%, followed by Agricultural Products and Services, Fertilizers and Agricultural Chemicals, and Packaged Foods and Meats. Pharmaceuticals are around 6.1% of assets, and Bayer takes a 6.14% slice as the #5 position. Each US$1,000 in KROP allocates about US$61 to Bayer, with the rest spread across stocks such as Deere and Nutrien. About 41% of KROP overlaps MOO. However, KROP allocates more of its assets to precision farming, inputs providers and food-focused companies that MOO does not emphasise in the same way.

Bayer faces the risk that its returns on invested capital and earnings could be pressured over the near and medium term. KROP still leaves you tied to similar agriculture and inputs themes through holdings like Deere and Nutrien, although those depend on different parts of the farm economy than Bayer. This structure means your view on Bayer is partly cushioned by other agriculture-related businesses and still depends on the broader food and farming cycle remaining attractive enough to support that group as a whole.

Bayer through funds means choosing your mix

If you want Bayer in size, MOO gives you the biggest slice, about US$92 in Bayer for every US$1,000. It also carries the highest fee at roughly US$56 a year on a US$10,000 holding. KROP sits in the middle with roughly US$61 in Bayer per US$1,000 and a portfolio tilted toward farming equipment and inputs rather than broad resources. HAP spreads you across 148 holdings, the widest set here, with about US$42 in Bayer per US$1,000 and the lowest annual cost at about US$41 on US$10,000.

The licensing deal for Bayer’s new cancer drug adds interest, but earnings could still come under pressure. Your choice is whether you want a concentrated agriculture tilt with MOO or KROP, or a more mixed resource and power portfolio with HAP where Bayer is a smaller piece.

data.title: Learn Why The Bull Case For Ero Copper Stock Could Change Following Tucuma Production Halt
data.description:
• Ero Copper has temporarily halted all mining and processing at the Tucumã Operation after overflow incidents during heavy El Niño driven rainfall led regulators to find anomalous pH levels in nearby water and order a production shutdown, pending approval of a remediation plan.
  • The operational pause at Tucumã introduces fresh execution and cost pressure at a time when Ero Copper is pursuing long term efficiency programs and preparing for larger growth projects that depend on stable Brazilian permitting and environmental compliance.
  • We will examine how Ero Copper's investment narrative is being tested by the Tucumã shutdown that followed anomalous pH readings in local water.
Spot check how the Ero Copper story compares by scanning a curated list of copper producers with solid fundamentals using the 16 top copper producer stocks.

Ero Copper Investment Narrative Recap

To own Ero Copper, you need to be comfortable with a Brazil focused copper and gold producer that is still in a build out phase. The analyst consensus narrative on Simply Wall St leans heavily on OneEro efficiency work at Caraíba, Tucumã and Xavantina, plus potential future growth from Furnas. The Tucumã halt directly affects current copper output and near term cash generation, so it sits squarely against that operational ramp up story.

In the short term, the key catalyst is a clean, regulator approved remediation plan that allows Tucumã production to restart and keep Brazilian permitting onside. The biggest risk right now is that operational interruptions and remediation costs stack on top of existing execution issues such as past guidance revisions and higher input costs. Combined, these factors could strain margins and delay funding flexibility for Furnas and other projects.

The most relevant recent development is the formal suspension of all production activities at Tucumã, along with the roughly US$2.9 million environmental fine linked to the overflow incidents. That is not a balance sheet breaking number for a CA$3.3b company, but it is a clear flag that regulatory compliance is front and centre for Ero Copper’s mine plan.

Options data highlighted elevated implied volatility on a January 2027 call, which indicates traders are positioning for sizable share price swings around catalysts such as this restart process. For individual investors, the focus is more basic. Monitor how quickly Ero Copper secures SEMAS approval, how any new operating conditions affect Tucumã’s cost structure, and what that means for funding capacity for OneEro programs and the long dated Furnas development plans.

Ero Copper's narrative projects $1.4b revenue and $436.5 million earnings by 2029. This assumes 9.0% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about $125 million from $311.3 million today.
